source.title: Gradings, Braidings, Representations, Paraparticles: Some Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Over the complex numbers, classify all gradings of the paraparticle algebras and coalgebras called the Relative Parabose Set P_BF and the Relative Parafermi Set P_FB by small finite abelian groups. Equivalently, determine all group actions or coactions, or actions/coactions of the group Hopf algebra C G, that preserve the algebra and coalgebra structures so that these objects become C G-module or C G-comodule algebras and coalgebras.
accepted.context_brief: Finite-group gradings of mixed paraparticle algebras

accepted.question_text: For each grading of P_BF or P_FB by a small finite abelian group G, classify all compatible braided group structures. This means determining the possible bicharacters, equivalently commutation factors or color functions, the corresponding universal R-matrices of the group Hopf algebra C G, and the corresponding braidings of the C G-module or C G-comodule categories, and then deciding which choices admit compatible graded algebra and coalgebra structures that make the paraparticle algebra into a braided group.

For the graded and braided paraparticle Hopf structures arising from small finite abelian group gradings and compatible braidings of the mixed paraparticle algebras P_BF and P_FB, can bosonization or bosonization-like methods be applied or developed to produce ordinary Hopf structures with no grading and trivial braiding while preserving equivalent representation theories?

For the free parabosonic algebra P_B and the free parafermionic algebra P_F with infinitely many degrees of freedom, can the braided Green-ansatz tensor-product method be completed to explicitly construct Fock-like representations by computing generator actions and matrix elements? In the parabosonic case, this requires a suitable multinomial theorem for the anticommuting variables that appear in the graded tensor-product representation.

When the graded tensor-product representations constructed by the braided Green-ansatz method for paraparticle algebras are decomposed into irreducible components, do they contain irreducible direct summands or submodules other than the known p-Fock-like modules?

Can the braided tensor-product construction for P_B and P_F be generalized to the mixed paraparticle algebras P_BF and P_FB, where P_BF is the Relative Parabose Set and P_FB is the Relative Parafermi Set mixing parabosonic and parafermionic degrees of freedom? This asks whether Fock-like representations of P_BF and P_FB can be extracted as irreducible submodules from graded tensor-product representations of suitable symmetric and antisymmetric Clifford-Weyl quotient algebras, and whether one can develop a multinomial theorem mixing commuting and anticommuting variables.

Do the proposed Hamiltonians built from a monochromatic parabosonic field and a (p+1)-level system, with spectrum-generating algebra P_BF(1,1), P_FB(1,1), or a related mixed paraparticle algebra, yield exactly solvable generalizations of the Jaynes-Cummings model whose energy levels, eigenfunctions, transition rates, and other physical quantities can be computed and compared with theory and experiment?

trace.notes: Normalized the single input URL as a zbMATH resolver. Local shell fetches to zbmath.org and api.zbmath.org failed with DNS resolution errors in the sandbox, so exact-work local resolver metadata was used to identify the title, DOI 10.3390/axioms1010074, and arXiv link 1210.2348. Exact-title web recovery found the MDPI full HTML article, whose visible body contains the problem statements, and extraction used that HTML source.

Mapped the article structure: Abstract; 1 Introduction; 1.1 Structure of the Paper; 2 The Algebras; 3 Braided Group, Ordinary Hopf and Lie Structures; 3.1 conceptual background; 4 representation construction; 4.2 research objectives; 5 Hamiltonian model; 5.2 research objectives; 6 Conclusions. Key terminology includes paraparticle algebras P_B, P_F, P_BF, P_FB, small finite abelian group gradings, C G-module/comodule structures, bicharacters, universal R-matrices, braided groups, Fock-like representations, symmetric and antisymmetric Clifford-Weyl algebras, and paraparticle Jaynes-Cummings-type Hamiltonians. The likely open-problem regions are Sections 3.2, 4.2, and 5.2.
